claims.claim: Kotlin Analysis API compiler semantics are parameterized by platform-supplied module/project structure, so compiler reuse does not make the frontend authoritative for build context.
Kotlin FIR/Analysis API obtains interactive value from lazy frontend resolution plus cached, explicitly invalidated session state rather than process persistence alone.
Kotlin generated/plugin declarations can participate semantically inside resolution and carry their own invalidation/collision rules, which file-only orchestration cannot generally reconstruct.

SourceKit-LSP deliberately delegates build targets, source membership, compiler options, preparation, and build-change freshness to an external build server while using sourcekitd for Swift semantics.
SourceKit owns snapshot-qualified reusable AST state, while the LSP layer separately owns failure recovery and process restart.

For Anneal, build/environment/generated-artifact authority can remain orchestration-owned, while upstream services are justified when interaction requires semantic state only the upstream engine can safely maintain.
evidence: All Kotlin and Swift evidence above
claims.reasoning: Both ecosystems preserve an external project/build authority while placing lazy/reusable semantic state inside the compiler frontend. The split maps to Anneal's need for explicit verification identity: service-local caches can accelerate a named context without becoming authority for which context or result is accepted.

negative_evidence: No execution or benchmark was performed.
No source establishes a universal performance threshold for daemonizing an analysis stage.
Kotlin plugin-generated semantics are not assumed to be generally materializable as source files.
SourceKit-LSP build-tool support is not generalized to every Swift/Xcode build integration.
Anneal implications are derived and conditional, not project policy.
